artworks.title: Long-tailed Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows several long-tailed ducks. Two ducks are perched on rocks above the water, while three ducklings and one duck are swimming in the water. The ducks have a palette of browns, whites, and black with long tails. The largest duck stands on the left rock, angled towards the viewer, while the other adult duck is on the right rock. In the water below, one duck is swimming close to the center, followed by three ducklings. The background shows a calm sea and a pale sky.

artworks.title: Blue-winged Teal
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two blue-winged teals in flight. The artwork depicts two teal ducks gliding in the sky, with a background of a landscape featuring water and hills. Both ducks have blue patches on their wings, with one showing mottled brown and blue plumage, while the other has orange underbelly and a blue and white face pattern. Their bodies are elongated to suggest motion, and their feet are outstretched. The landscape has tones of green and slate. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for precise illustrations of birds.

artworks.title: Black-headed Gull
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two gulls. The painting depicts two birds, one with a black and white head and red legs in the foreground, while the other in the background is more subdued in color. The primary bird is perched with a forward gaze, showcasing its feathers with precise line work and shading. Both birds rest on an earthy surface.

artworks.title: Red-breasted Sandpiper
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two sandpipers on a rocky shoreline with water and mountains in the background. The artwork shows two birds prominently; the one in the foreground has a red-orange plumage on its breast, with patterns of brown, black, and white on its wings and back. Beside it is another bird with a color palette of grays and whites, both standing on a rock ledge jutting into calm water. The backdrop reveals a smooth horizon with mountains under a pale blue sky. It is in the style of John James Audubon, known for detailed depictions of birds. The painting exemplifies attention to detail and accurate representation of the birds’ physical characteristics in a serene natural setting.

artworks.title: Black-bellied Darter
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a tree stump by the water. The painting depicts a pair of waterfowl, identified as the Black-bellied Darter, scientifically known as Plotus Anhinga, standing atop a weathered tree trunk. One bird is perched higher than the other, with its wings outstretched, displaying intricate feather patterns in dark and light shades of black and grey. The other bird, sitting below, has a distinctive long neck, and its body is colored with rich brown and navy blue plumage. Its feet are bright yellow, gripping the bark of the trunk. In the background, there's a serene body of water with reflections of trees and a soft, peach-colored sky. This painting is reminiscent of John James Audubon's style, known for his detailed illustrations of birds.

artworks.title: Black or Surf Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two large ducks are depicted in a coastal setting. One duck is standing on a rock, while the other is on the sandy ground next to seashells. The ducks are primarily black and brown in color, with the background showing peach and blue tones. The duck on the left is on a rock, while the duck on the right is on the sandy shore.

artworks.title: American Avocet
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of an American Avocet in its natural habitat. The scene features the bird foraging at the edge of a body of water, surrounded by greenery and rocks. The American Avocet is shown with its long legs, slender bill, and vibrant plumage. In the background, there are other birds near the water, with more visible further back. The setting includes lush foliage and calm water, creating a wetland atmosphere.

artworks.title: Lesser Tern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds in flight against a dark background. The image depicts two terns with detailed feathering and graceful forms. One bird is in a downward gliding posture with folded wings, while the other bird has wings spread wide. The background is a dark, muted blue contrasting with the white tones of the terns.

artworks.title: Little Sandpiper
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two sandpipers near a stream, set against a backdrop of lush trees. The birds display detailed brown and white plumage as they stand by the water's edge. Trees obscure the horizon, and the stream winds its way from the background. The painting features precise brushstrokes, capturing the details of the birds and scenery. The color scheme includes earthy browns and greens for the vegetation, complemented by soft blue water and a pale, peachy sky.

artworks.title: Roseate Spoonbill
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This print shows a side view of a pink bird with its wings slightly outstretched, perched on a sloped brown bank with its head leaning down toward the water on the left. The bird has a long, white neck, a green head with red eyes surrounded by circles of pink, and a large beak that flares out at the end, similar to a spoon. The beak has white and black patterns on the top, which fade into a light blue at the bottom. The wings, legs, body, and feet of the bird are pink.  In the background on the left, the horizon is in the center of the painting, revealing a wetland landscape with blue water and patches of green land. On the right, there is a patch of tall green grass behind the bird. The sky has soft gray clouds against a pale-yellow sky.

artworks.title: Red-Headed Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two red-headed ducks on a riverbank surrounded by grass. One duck is standing alert with its head raised, showcasing its vibrant red head and a body clad in shades of black, gray, and white. The duck's webbed feet are prominently displayed, adding a sense of movement. Beside it, another duck sits calmly, adorned with earthier tones and a textured pattern on its feathers. Delicate strokes illustrate the grasses bending gently. The scene is under a soft pastel sky. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Black Skimmer
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paperr
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a black skimmer bird in flight over the ocean. The painting captures the bird with its long, black wings which contrast against its white underbelly, and a bright red bill that is slightly open as it skims the surface of the sea. The ocean beneath the bird has subtle waves, while the sky above has a serene gradient of blues and grays. The painting exemplifies detailed and naturalistic representation, commonly associated with ornithological illustrations. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Bonapartian Gull
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows three gulls by the sea with a cloudy backdrop. Two gulls are on a rocky shore, one with a dark head and the other with a light head, while a third gull is flying above them. The birds are depicted realistically, showcasing the detailed patterns and colors of their feathers, as well as their natural poses. In the background, the sea meets distant cliffs under a sky with dynamic cloud formations. It is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Buffel-headed Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: There are two ducks in the image. One duck is standing and the other is resting on the ground. The standing duck has black and white plumage with an iridescent green patch on its head. The resting duck has darker plumage with a white underside and a similar iridescent spot on its head. The background shows green grass and a patch of earth, with a soft, pale sky. The resting duck is on the left and the standing duck is on the right.

artworks.title: Gannet
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting features two seabirds in a coastal setting. One bird in the foreground is preening its feathers, while the other bird in the background has its head turned upwards. The foreground bird has grey and white plumage with green webbed feet, and the background bird has a white and orange head. They are perched on rocky terrain near a turbulent sea, under a sky filled with flying seabirds and clouds. The composition emphasizes the textures of the birds' feathers and the rugged seascape. This artwork is reminiscent of John James Audubon's detailed bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Shoveller Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two ducks are portrayed in a natural setting. The painting features two ducks on a rocky surface near a small body of water, surrounded by tall grasses. The left duck has colorful plumage with blues, greens, and browns, while the right duck has a more muted color palette of browns and greys. Both ducks have their necks outstretched and their beaks open. The environment is lush with green reeds. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Long-legged Avocet
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image features a bird with red legs standing on rocks near a calm body of water. The bird has a black and white body, and balances on one leg. The background shows a sky with grey clouds blending into a pastel blue hue. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Yellow-breasted Rail
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image presents a side view of a yellow-breasted rail on a rocky outcrop. The background shows a water-lined landscape with trees. The art style is highly detailed with precise lines defining the bird's feathers, rocks, and grass. The colors are natural and vibrant, with warm browns and oranges of the bird's plumage contrasting against the cooler blues of the sky and water.

artworks.title: Ring Plover
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds identified as the "King Plover, Charadrius Semipalmatus." One bird is standing on the right, displaying rich brown and white plumage with a black band across its chest. The other bird on the left appears to be focused downward, with its beak close to the ground, possibly searching for food among the rocks. The setting features grasses and water in the background, bordered by distant hills under a serene sky. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Goosander
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two ducks by a waterfall. There are two ducks, one standing on a rock with green reeds nearby, and the other swimming in the water. The background shows cascading waterfalls and a serene landscape. The standing duck has a deep green head, dark markings, and pink feet, while the swimming duck has brown and grey feathers and a rusty head. The background features gently flowing water and distant greenery.

artworks.title: Pied Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two ducks by a coastal landscape. The painting shows two ducks perched on a rocky outcrop by the water. The duck on the left has a brown head with bluish feathers covering its body, while the duck on the right has white and black plumage, extending its wings. The background features a gradient sky transitioning from pastel blues to pinkish hues over a calm sea with distant cliffs.

artworks.title: Green Heron
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two Green Herons among vegetation, observing a butterfly. The composition features the herons in a natural setting with green leaves and a rocky stream. One heron is in a dynamic pose with its beak aimed at the butterfly, while the other heron stands gracefully. A pastel-colored butterfly sits on a leaf above them. The background is detailed, creating a lush environment. This artwork is similar to John James Audubon's style.

artworks.title: Black-bellied Plover
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Three birds are depicted on a rocky ground in the image. The central bird has intricate black and white patterns on its body and wings. The bird on the left has brown and white plumage, while the bird on the right has brown, white, and black colors. Earthy tones like browns, blacks, and grays are present, with a hint of light blue in the background. The arrangement shows the largest bird in the center, a bird in the foreground on the right, and the tallest bird positioned behind the central bird and to the left.

artworks.title: Red-breasted Snipe
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two red-breasted snipes. The painting depicts two snipes on the banks of a body of water. The bird in the foreground has a vividly patterned brown and white plumage, with its head lowered. Its wings and tail show intricate feather detailing. The other bird stands upright, showcasing its reddish-brown breast and darker, speckled feather patterns on its back and tail. Behind them, a landscape of water and scattered rocks fades into the distance, with a soft gradient sky.
